review_description: The sales process was excellent with no doubts in progressing with the installation. Installation is of a high standard with a neat and tidy result. The paper work trail was exceptional with PSW put no pressure on me to sign up. other suppliers where giving huge a sense of urgency for what where large install lead times. Very punctual in relation to quoting, installation and demonstrating the system.
Sales and Quoting process was excellent, couldn't fault them one bit. Even after excepting the quote their follow up has been 5 Star. Haven't had it installed yet so can't comment.

Initial solar install:I contacted them telling them exactly what system I wanted. They took a while to respond. I said "Yes, install". They took 2 weeks to get back to me and ask for confirmation, resulting in my install being in the new calendar year and therefore decreased rebates. They sent me the wrong invoice/contract the first time and I had to chase them up to ensure I was getting the right system installed. Even after 'fixing' the contract still stated different items to what I actually got (and wanted) installed.Battery install:This is where their customer service has been absolutely appalling. I asked for a new customer service rep from the first time. I can't even remember all the issues... They've been on holiday, then sick, then just not responding. At no point was I informed. I've asked questions that have been left with no reply for months. I chase up every other month to get crickets. I've contacted their main office who has supposedly "gone downstairs and spoken to him just now" and still nothing. My questions are unanswered. And my install has once again been pushed out until the new calendar year.I contacted them the minute battery rebates were confirmed to be occurring. I was initially booked for 1st July as I was so fast in. I said I wanted to go the "interest free loan" route, and so they moved me back to allow time for that. And back again. And back again. And Oh dear there's no batteries in stock, you're now 6th of January.I've now spent the last 2 weeks sending my rep "is this still the best option?" followed by "heeeellllo?" "Heeeeeeelllllooooo" to no reply.Don't use this place if you have any questions, and/or aren't willing to be constantly and aggressively pursuing them to get things done.
To fully understand what I was getting I visited the business to discuss in person.

Highly recommend PSW Energy for their quality products, service, and after-sales support.

Initially got a quote (and booked installation) for an Alpha Gen2 13.3kWh battery installed for $8990. WA rebate was to be $5000. Out of pocket $3990.Fast forward a couple of months, WA changed their rebate to $1300, but Federal Govt was also providing a rebate.2 weeks before install, their admin team sent a reminder of the install, what is to be installed, an invoice for the total amount (no rebate deducted) and a statement saying I had to pay it on the day on installation otherwise the battery wouldn't be activated.I reached out to PSW as I was under the impression the installer handled the rebate and it should come off the invoice total, plus there was no mention of the rebate changes or VPP for WA. Sales got back to me within a few hours, advising of the updated rebates, but also that the initial battery we had ordered was no longer available - huh? I just received an invoice stating I was being charged for it. How would this have played out if I never reached out asking about the rebate? They did say that if I wanted, I could get a "complementary upgrade" at "no additional cost" to a newer generation 15kWh battery - newer and larger upgrade for free!Turns out "complementary upgrade" at "no additional cost" is actually the cost increasing by $630; going from $8990 to $9620. But I guess in their eyes, as the rebate increased by $1620 ($1300 + $5320 vs $5000) due to a larger battery, there is no cost increase. Sure, my out of pocket hasn't increased, but the lure of a free upgrade at no cost increase, when there is a cost increase, just isn't right. Just say, "a newer battery with larger capacity will cost more, but you'll get more rebate back, so you won't be out of pocket any extra". Perhaps I'm being a little too pedantic on terminology? But words have meaning and the contracts they have you sign are very strict on the terminology used.My interactions with the company to date have been with sales staff and admin staff. Apart from the terminology/lures mentioned, the interactions with sales staff have been great. They were really prompt in getting back to me when I had questions.The admin staff, not so much. The first email they sent mentioned to reply if there were questions, but they never replied to questions; along with sending an invoice for a product they no longer had + failing to include rebates they are meant to administer...just felt lacking with the proficiency side of things. I had to do the prompting for rebate and VPP info, and then it was sales staff who answered. I would expect the admin staff to be all over those aspects of the business and be proactive with sharing information on it; some customers may not even beware of what questions to ask, but sadly the proactiveness is lacking.If you're not picky about those types of things, then you shouldn't have any problems.

I obtained a total of 4 quotes (all from companies with good reviews on SolarQuotes) in February 2025, PSW's quote was by far the cheapest. Obtaining quotes for different brands of panels and inverters from PSW was easy and by far the most transparent and straightforward because after we have agreed on the system size, they simply sent me a link listing their available products and price for me to choose from. The other reason why I chose PSW was that they offered an installation date within a week from signing the contract, as opposed to a 3-6 weeks wait as offered by other companies.PSW sent a team of two friendly electricians (contractors) to complete the job. They gave us options as to where we would like the inverter to be installed. They cleaned up after the job was done, gave a brief introduction on how to use the inverter, and answered all my questions. I am happy with the installation team and their work.One hiccup in this shopping experience was that although I raised the same concern of limited roof area to the four companies I obtained quotes from, only one salesman (not from PSW) addressed my concern and appropriately offered an alternative solar panel layout plan. The other three salesman were over-confident that all 15 panels could be installed on the second storey roof. Eventually, on the day of installation, the electricians measured my roof and proposed to install 7 panels on the second storey roof, while 8 panels will be installed on the first storey roof. Immediately I raised my concern that the proposed first storey roof is permanently shaded by the second storey in the morning, and shaded by my neighbour's line of trees bordering the lot in the evening. After some communication, the electricians offered to installing 11 panels on the second storey roof, and only leave 4 panels on the first storey roof, despite the morning shade, to which we agreed. I suspect this panel layout might have cost the team more time and cost to install, but they were willing to make this adjustment in order to maximise solar production in the long run, which I really appreciate. This shows the importance of being on-site and be ready to discuss with the electricians, as initially planning was inaccurate, and no shade analysis was done at the time of sales (not just for PSW, but for other solar companies as well).Other than that I am happy with the purchase and PSW's after-sales customer service was good!

It would appear that a 3 phase installation with a Powerwall is not that common in Perth (back in January).The system has worked flawlessly (except for a minor hiccup during a power outage, but this appears to have has been rectified), so I am very happy with the end solution and installation.  To date the system is performing better than my forecast; I have saved over $1050 in electricity costs in 6 months and expect a payback for the whole system in about 9 years.  Electricity bill for the 6 months was $80 inc. GST.  BTW, I get 0 cents credit from Western Power for input to the Grid, because I have a 10kwh inverter.  I would get whole 3 cents if I only had a 5kwh inverter.Things that weren’t obvious to me at the start, but is my fault for not investigating further:•	A single Powerwall can only support 1 phase.  2 Powerwalls can support 2 phases if configured that way, but only one works during a Grid outage.•	Western Power (via Tesla) limits the input/output of the Powerwall to 3kwh. This can impact the charge on very cloudy days.•	If the Grid goes down during the day, the Solar array stops as well because the inverter needs power to all 3 phases (the Powerwall only supports 1 phase).Would I recommend PSW?  Yes, definitely, but be prepared to do some fairly rigorous investigations yourself if you want a non-typical install (ie. not a 6kw solar only system).  I suspect this would be the case with most if not all installers.  I went with PSW because they provided a competitive price, quality service, were local and only used trained employees to do the installation.
